turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about the last time you switched how your team tracks customer feedback.

turns.speaker: participant
turns.text: That was in September. We had feedback scattered across email and a shared spreadsheet, and in a roadmap review I couldn't find the three complaints about exports that a customer had sent.

turns.speaker: participant
turns.text: I started looking at tools that night. Honestly I kept hoping the spreadsheet would hold up, because everyone already knew how to use it and changing it felt like a big deal.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What made you pick that one in the end?

turns.speaker: participant
turns.text: The demo showed every complaint tagged to the customer and the date, so I could see all export complaints in one view. But I worried the team wouldn't tag things consistently and it would end up just as messy.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Walk me through the first week using it.

turns.speaker: participant
turns.text: I imported the spreadsheet on a Tuesday. By Friday I could answer in a minute which customers had asked for exports, which was what I needed for the roadmap review.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Take me back to when you first thought about changing how you handle support tickets.

turns.speaker: participant
turns.text: It was after the outage in March. Customers emailed three different inboxes and we answered some twice and missed others, and my manager asked me why a refund took nine days.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What did you do about it?

turns.speaker: participant
turns.text: For two weeks I just added a rule to forward everything to one inbox. It sort of worked, and I knew how to maintain it, so I didn't want to start over.

turns.speaker: participant
turns.text: A colleague showed me her shared queue where each ticket had an owner. I wanted that: one place where nobody can claim a ticket without their name on it.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Was there anything that gave you pause?

turns.speaker: participant
turns.text: Not really. The price was fine and migration was one afternoon, I checked with their support before buying.
